title: VLA-Scope: Shift-Aware Failure Prediction for Vision-Language-Action Models
methods: logistic-regression OOD detector and 7-way shift-type classifier on mean-pooled image and text token embeddings of the first input
logistic-regression failure-risk predictor on 14 hand-crafted action-prefix features + predicted shift type + PCA-32 of the cumulative mean of last-layer last-prompt-token hidden states
question: Can combining the type of input shift, statistics of executed actions, and averaged hidden states predict whether an OpenVLA rollout under distribution shift will eventually fail?
key_findings: OOD detection from initial pooled embeddings: ROC-AUC 0.9454, TPR 84.57%, FPR 6.20%; shift-type accuracy 91.00% (macro-F1 0.9123); an ID-only cosine 1-NN baseline gets 0.8176 (Table I).
Text-only features detect OOD poorly (ROC-AUC 0.5714) but are needed for language shifts (detected Language-OOD cases rise from 18 to 170 of 200 when text is added).
Failure rate under shift ranges from 27.5% (Layout) to 77.5% (Camera); every category has both outcomes, so shift type alone does not determine failure.
Failure-risk ROC-AUC on all 1,400 OOD rollouts rises with steps: 0.6852 (step 10), 0.7675 (step 30), 0.8497 (step 60) on an unchanged cohort (Table II).
Ablation at step 60 (Table VI): without the cumulative hidden-state representation 0.7906; without action features 0.8344; action features alone 0.7756; predicted type alone 0.6739.
Baselines retrained on the same splits (Table IV, step 30 / 60): ActProbe 0.7601 / 0.8132, SAFE-MLP 0.7294 / 0.8055, SAFE-LSTM 0.6867 / 0.7414, VLA-Scope 0.7675 / 0.8497.
By step 60, an 'ever alarmed' rule catches 83.51% of failures but fires on 50.73% of successes, showing the operational false-alarm problem.

benchmarks: LIBERO-Spatial (10 tasks) with LIBERO-Plus perturbation categories and assets
evidence.scale: 50 ID + 20 OOD cases per category per task: 1,900 initial inputs, 1,400 OOD rollouts (751 successes, 649 failures); 10-fold leave-one-task-out CV; neural baselines averaged over 3 seeds
evidence.statistics: no: pooled held-out point estimates, no CIs or tests
evidence.baselines: ActProbe, SAFE-MLP, SAFE-LSTM retrained on same data; cosine 1-NN OOD baseline; action-only and instruction-context logistic variants

causal_validation: None; logistic weights decompose score changes into feature contributions, which the authors explicitly say describe the predictor, not physical failure causes.
closed_loop: Offline evaluation on recorded closed-loop rollouts; no intervention at runtime.
limitations_stated: OOD characterizer runs only at initialization, so shifts arising later are missed.
The OOD gate excludes 216 cases including 45 eventual failures that get no risk score.
Feature contributions describe score changes, not causes of failure.
critique: The hidden-state contribution is real but modest: removing the cumulative representation costs 0.059 ROC-AUC at step 60; most signal comes from simple action statistics (0.7756 alone).
The 'execution progress features' phrase in the abstract refers to averaged hidden states, not an explicit progress estimate; the naming is confusing.

Later-step and 'progress-based' results (ROC-AUC up to 0.98) are confounded by cohort change and episode length, since successes end early and failures run to the 220-action budget; the step-60 fixed-cohort number is the fair one, and the authors acknowledge the cohort issue.
The supervised OOD classifier is trained on the same seven perturbation families it is tested on (held-out task, not held-out perturbation), so 91% type accuracy says little about novel shifts.
Single model, single suite, simulation only, no seeds for the logistic models; comparisons to SAFE use retrained baselines on a different setting than SAFE's paper.
one_line: On 1,400 perturbed OpenVLA LIBERO rollouts, a logistic model combining a predicted shift type, simple action statistics and averaged last-layer hidden states predicts eventual failure (ROC-AUC 0.85 after 60 actions) better than SAFE and ActProbe, though hidden states add only about 0.06 over actions alone.
